title: Meiosis and Genetic Variation
seo_title: Meiosis Worksheets: Haploid Cells, Crossing Over and Variation (High School Biology)
standard_text: Ask questions to clarify relationships about the role of DNA and chromosomes in coding the instructions for characteristic traits passed from parents to offspring. Make and defend a claim based on evidence that inheritable genetic variations may result from new genetic combinations through meiosis, viable errors occurring during replication, and/or mutations caused by environmental factors.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on meiosis and genetic variation (NGSS HS-LS3-1, HS-LS3-2): chromosomes, haploid and diploid, stages of meiosis and sources of variation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Crossing over, independent assortment, fertilization and mutation make each offspring different.
body_html:
How to think about it

Meiosis makes gametes with half the chromosomes, each one different.

  • Diploid body cell (2n) → meiosis I and II → four haploid gametes (n).
  • Variation: crossing over, independent assortment (2n combinations), random fertilization and mutations.
  • Only mutations in gametes are inherited.
Example

Human 2n = 46. Sperm?

Halve it

Answer: 23

Example

3 chromosome pairs. Gamete combinations?

2^3

Answer: 8

Common mistakes

  • Thinking gametes have the full chromosome number.
  • Thinking meiosis makes two identical cells.
  • Thinking only mutations cause variation.

faq.q: How is meiosis different from mitosis?
faq.a: Meiosis has two divisions and makes four genetically different haploid cells. Mitosis has one division and makes two identical diploid cells.

faq.q: Where does genetic variation come from?
faq.a: Crossing over, independent assortment, random fertilization and mutations (replication errors or damage from the environment).
No. Only mutations in cells that make eggs or sperm can be passed to offspring.
